mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which may stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are not higher than baseline during easing periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If returns remain positive despite unemployment increases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If returns are negative despite housing growth.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production slowdown with strong retail sales indicates supply chain issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive despite supply chain issues.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate with inflation indicates tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive despite high rates and inflation.

mechanism_narrative: Employment growth without unemployment drop indicates tight labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth >0.5% MoM and UNRATE unchanged
failure_condition: If returns are negative despite labor market tightness.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production decline indicates economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive despite production decline.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth slowdown with high federal funds indicates stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive despite stagflation conditions.
